title: This Tiny Robot Just Did 10 Backflips in 11 Seconds!
summary:
Imagine a robot smaller than a paperclip, flipping through the air like a gymnast. That's what engineers at MIT just built. Their tiny flying robot, about the size of a microcassette, can now fly 450% faster than before. It can even do 10 backflips in 11 seconds!

The robot is called a microrobot. It has soft artificial muscles that flap its wings super fast, like a real insect. But flying fast and doing flips is hard. The robot needs a smart 'brain' to control its moves. So the team used AI to help it plan each flip and stay steady, even when wind pushes it.

Why does this matter? One day, these robots could help rescue people trapped under collapsed buildings after earthquakes. They can squeeze through small spaces where big drones can't go. 'We want to use these robots in places that are hard for traditional drones,' says Kevin Chen, a professor at MIT. 'Now our robot flies almost like a real insect.'

This is a big step toward robots that can search for people in disasters. And it's pretty cool to watch a robot do somersaults!
why_it_matters: This shows how science made for one problem — like flying like an insect — can later help save real people in disasters, maybe even in your own town.
